precedence: policies: project > personal > common; a locked common rule always wins

scopes.job: What the project is: description, created date, source control (repos), ticket control (Jira, Trello), environments, where the code graph is stored and how to query it (a pointer only), people and their roles, aliases. One row, edited in place.
scopes.write: kh_save(kind='about') or PUT /projects/{id}/about; never a second About row
scopes.read_when: choosing the project (after the hot log); summarised in the turn context

scopes.job: The project's mandatory rules. They win over the person's own and the common rules (locked common rules excepted).
scopes.read_when: injected once when the session binds or switches to the project

scopes.job: Business features, not code: overview nodes from module to component to step; each node points at the knowledge rows that spec it. The project's source of truth for what exists.
scopes.read_when: when a step names a feature, and in the task map (kh_task_full_retrieve)

scopes.job: Detailed spec chunks per feature node (metadata.node) and facts.
Work logs of the project (through the hot log).
scopes.read_when: questions about time, history or status

scopes.job: Open problems only: no concrete solution yet. A solved one moves to lessons.
scopes.write: POST /vector/add scope findings; solved: POST /findings/resolve {project, id, solution}
scopes.read_when: the turn context of the project

scopes.job: Solved findings with their solution, the corrections the person makes ('not like that, like this') and the lessons distilled from the work logs.
scopes.read_when: every prompt and every task map (kh_task_full_retrieve), by meaning, before knowledge

legacy: HOW THIS PROJECT WAS RUN BEFORE (layout legacy, made before 2026-11-03): its data was not moved. Policy rows may sit in kh_policy_<id> (read by /policy routes) besides kernel rules; lessons learned from work logs are distilled dk_* rows in knowledge (topic distilled); findings may hold resolved ones next to open ones (status field); the project card (knowledge, topic project-card) and entity cards (scope entity) still hold facts and people; a code graph, if any, is in kh_src_<id> and the project graph. New writes follow the seven scopes (GET /projects/<id>/layout).
